collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Definitions

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Establishment of Advisory Council for Occupational Health and Safety
body: There is hereby established an Advisory Council for Occupational Health and Safety.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Functions of Council

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Constitution of Council

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Period of office and remuneration of members of Council
body:
(1) The members of the Council referred to in section 4(2) shall be appointed for a period of three years, and on such conditions as the Minister may determine.
(2) Any person whose period of office as a member of the Council has expired shall be eligible for reappointment.
(3) A member referred to in section 4(1)(f), (g), (h), (i) or (j) who is not an officer may be paid from money appropriated for such purpose by Parliament such allowances as the Minister may determine.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Establishment of technical committees of Council
body:
(1) The Council may with the approval of the Minister establish one or more technical committees to advise the Council on any matter regarding the performance by the Council of its functions.
(2) A member of a technical committee shall be appointed by the Council by reason of his knowledge of the matter for which the committee is established, and such a member need not be a member of the Council.
(3) A meeting of a technical committee shall be held at such time and place as may be determined by the chairman of the Council, and in accordance with rules approved by the Council.
(4) A member of a technical committee who is not an officer may be paid from money appropriated for such purpose by Parliament such allowances as the Minister may determine.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Health and safety policy
body:
(1) The chief inspector may direct any employer in writing, and any category of employers by notice in the Gazette, to prepare a written policy concerning the protection of the health and safety of his employees at work, including a description of his organization and the arrangements for carrying out and reviewing that policy.
(2) Any direction under subsection (1) shall be accompanied by guide-lines concerning the contents of the policy concerned.
(3) An employer shall prominently display a copy of the policy referred to in subsection (1), signed by the chief executive officer, in the workplace where his employees normally report for service.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: General duties of employers to their employees

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: General duties of employers and self-employed persons to persons other than their employees
body:
(1) Every employer shall conduct his undertaking in such a manner as to ensure, as far as is reasonably practicable, that persons other than those in his employment who may be directly affected by his activities are not thereby exposed to hazards to their health or safety.
(2) Every self-employed person shall conduct his undertaking in such a manner as to ensure, as far as is reasonably practicable, that he and other persons who may be directly affected by his activities are not thereby exposed to hazards to their health or safety.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: General duties of manufacturers and others regarding articles and substances for use at work
body:
(1) Any person who designs, manufactures, imports, sells or supplies any article for use at work shall ensure, as far as is reasonably practicable, that the article is safe and without risks to health when properly used and that it complies with all prescribed requirements.
(2) Any person who erects or installs any article for use at work shall ensure, as far as is reasonably practicable, that nothing about the manner in which it is erected or installed makes it unsafe or creates a risk to health when properly used.
(3) Any person who manufactures, imports, sells or supplies any substance for use at work shall—
(a) ensure, as far as is reasonably practicable, that the substance is safe and without risks to health when properly used; and
(b) take such steps as may be necessary to ensure that information is available with regard to the use of the substance at work, the risks to health and safety associated with such substance, and the procedures to be followed in the case of an accident involving such substance.
(4) Where a person designs, manufactures, imports, sells or supplies an article or substance and that other person undertakes in writing to take specified steps sufficient to ensure that the article or substance will comply with all prescribed requirements, the undertaking shall have the effect of relieving the first-mentioned person from the duty imposed upon him by this section to such an extent as may be reasonable.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Listed work
body:
(1) The Minister may, subject to the provisions of subsections (2) and (3), by notice in the Gazette declare any work, under the conditions or circumstances specified in the notice, to be listed work.
(2) (a) Before the Minister declares any work to be listed work, he shall cause to be published in the Gazette a draft of his proposed notice and invite interested persons to submit comments and representations.
(b) A period of not less than three months shall elapse between the publication of the draft notice and the notice under subsection (1).
(3) The provisions of subsection (2) shall not apply if the Minister decides to publish the notice in an amended form, or where the public interest requires that it be made without delay.
(4) A notice under subsection (1) may at any time be amended or withdrawn by like notice.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: General duties of employers regarding listed work
body:
(1) Subject to such arrangements as may be prescribed, every employer whose employees undertake listed work or are liable to be exposed to the hazards emanating from listed work, shall, after consultation with the health and safety committee established for that workplace—
(a) identify the hazards and evaluate the risks associated with such work constituting a hazard to the health of such employees, and the steps that need to be taken to comply with the provisions of this Act;
(b) as far as is reasonably practicable, prevent the exposure of such employees to the hazards concerned or, where prevention is not reasonably practicable, minimize such exposure; and
(c) having regard to the nature of the risks associated with such work, carry out an occupational hygiene programme and biological monitoring, and subject such employees to medical surveillance.
(2) Every employer contemplated in subsection (1) shall keep the health and safety representatives informed of the actions taken and their results: Provided that individual results of biological monitoring and medical surveillance shall only with the written consent of the employee be made available to any person other than an inspector, the employer or the employee concerned.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Duty to inform
body:
Without derogating from any specific duty imposed on an employer by this Act, every employer shall—
(a) as far as is reasonably practicable, cause every employee to be made conversant with the hazards to his health and safety attached to any work which he has to perform, as well as the precautionary measures which should be taken and observed with respect to those hazards;
(b) inform the health and safety representatives concerned beforehand of inspections, investigations or formal inquiries of which he has been notified by an inspector, and of any application for exemption made by him in terms of section 40; and
(c) inform a health and safety representative as soon as reasonably practicable of the occurrence of an incident in the workplace or section of the workplace for which such representative has been designated.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: General duties of employees at work

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Duty not to interfere with, damage or misuse things
body: No person shall intentionally or recklessly interfere with, damage or misuse anything which is provided in the interest of health or safety.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Chief executive officer charged with certain duties
body:
(1) Every chief executive officer shall as far as is reasonably practicable ensure that the duties of his employer as contemplated in this Act, are properly discharged.
(2) Without derogating from his responsibility or liability in terms of subsection (1), a chief executive officer may assign any duty contemplated in the said subsection, to any person under his control, which person shall act subject to the control and directions of the chief executive officer.
(3) The provisions of subsection (1) shall not, subject to the provisions of section 37, relieve an employer of any responsibility or liability under this Act.
(4) For the purpose of subsection (1), the head of department of any department of State shall be deemed to be the chief executive officer of that department.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Health and safety representatives
body:
(1) Subject to the provisions of subsection (2), every employer who has more than 20 employees in his employment at any workplace, shall designate in writing for a specified period health and safety representatives for such workplace, or for different sections thereof.
(2) An employer and the representatives of his employees shall consult in good faith regarding the arrangements and procedures for the nomination or election, period of office and subsequent designation of health and safety representatives: Provided that if such consultation fails, the matter shall be referred for arbitration to a person mutually agreed upon, whose decision shall be final.
(3) Arbitration in terms of subsection (2) shall not be subject to the provisions of the Arbitration Act, 1965, and a failure of the consultation contemplated in that subsection shall not be deemed to be a dispute in terms of the Labour Relations Act, 1956.
(4) Only those employees employed in a full-time capacity at a specific workplace and who are acquainted with conditions and activities at that workplace shall be eligible for designation as health and safety representatives for that workplace.
(5) The number of health and safety representatives for a workplace shall in the case of shops and offices be at least one for every 100 employees or part thereof, and in the case of all other workplaces at least one for every 50 employees or part thereof.
(6) If an inspector is of the opinion that the number of health and safety representatives for any workplace is inadequate, he may by notice in writing direct the employer to designate such number of employees as the inspector may determine.
(7) All activities in connection with the designation, functions and training of health and safety representatives shall be performed during ordinary working hours, and any time reasonably spent by any employee in this regard shall be deemed to be time spent by him in the carrying out of his duties as an employee.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Functions of health and safety representatives

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Health and safety committees
body:
(1) An employer shall in respect of each workplace where two or more health and safety representatives have been designated, establish one or more health and safety committees and consult with the committee with a view to initiating, developing, promoting, maintaining and reviewing measures to ensure the health and safety of his employees at work.
(2) A health and safety committee shall consist of such number of members as the employer may from time to time determine, provided that all health and safety representatives for a workplace shall be members of the committee, and that the number of persons nominated by an employer shall not exceed the number of health and safety representatives.
(3) The persons nominated by an employer on a health and safety committee shall be designated in writing by the employer for such period as may be determined by him.
(4) A health and safety committee shall hold meetings as often as may be necessary, but at least once every three months, at a time and place determined by the committee.
(5) The procedure at meetings of a health and safety committee shall be determined by the committee.
(6) A health and safety committee may co-opt one or more persons by reason of his or their particular knowledge of health or safety matters as an advisory member or members of the committee, who shall not be entitled to vote.
(7) If an inspector is of the opinion that the number of health and safety committees established for any particular workplace is inadequate, he may in writing direct the employer to establish such number of health and safety committees as the inspector may determine.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Functions of health and safety committees
body:
(1) A health and safety committee—
(a) may make recommendations to the employer or, where the recommendations fail to resolve the matter, to an inspector regarding any matter affecting the health or safety of persons at the workplace;
(b) shall discuss any incident at the workplace in which any person was injured, became ill or died, and may in writing report on the incident to an inspector; and
(c) shall perform such other functions as may be prescribed.
(2) A health and safety committee shall keep record of each recommendation made to an employer and of any report made to an inspector.
(3) A health and safety committee or a member thereof shall not incur any civil liability by reason of the fact only that it or he failed to do anything which it or he may or is required to do in terms of this Act.
(4) An employer shall take the prescribed steps to ensure that a health and safety committee complies with the provisions of section 19(4) and performs the duties assigned to it.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: General prohibitions
body:
(1) The Minister may by notice in the Gazette declare—
(a) that no employer shall require or permit any employee belonging to a category of employees specified in the notice to perform work on or in any premises on or in which an activity specified in the notice is carried out which threatens the health or safety of an employee, otherwise than on the conditions specified in the notice;
(b) that no employer shall require or permit any employee to perform any work in connection with a process specified in the notice which threatens the health or safety of an employee, otherwise than on the conditions specified in the notice; and
(c) that no employer shall require or permit any employee, otherwise than on the conditions specified in the notice, to perform any work on or in any premises where an article or substance specified in the notice is produced, processed, used, handled, stored or transported which threatens the health or safety of an employee.
(2) The Minister shall, before he publishes a notice under subsection (1), cause a draft of his proposed notice to be published in the Gazette and invite interested persons to submit comments and representations.
(3) A notice under subsection (1) may at any time be amended or withdrawn by like notice.
(4) A notice shall not be issued under subsection (1) or (3) unless the Minister for National Health and Welfare and the Council have been consulted.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Sale of certain articles prohibited
body: Subject to the provisions of section 10(4), if any requirement (including any health and safety standard) in respect of any article, substance, plant, machinery or health and safety equipment has been prescribed, no person shall sell or market in any manner whatsoever such article, substance, plant, machinery or health and safety equipment unless it complies with that requirement.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Certain deductions prohibited
body: No employer shall in respect of anything which he is in terms of this Act required to provide or to do in the interest of the health or safety of an employee, make any deduction from any employee's remuneration or require or permit any employee to make any payment to him or any other person.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Report to inspector regarding certain incidents
body:
(1) Each incident occurring at work or arising out of or in connection with the activities of persons at work, or in connection with the use of plant or machinery, in which, or in consequence of which—
(a) any person dies, becomes unconscious, suffers the loss of a limb or part of a limb or is otherwise injured or becomes ill to such a degree that he is likely either to die or to suffer a permanent physical defect or is likely to be unable for a period of at least 14 days either to work or to continue with the activity for which he was employed;
(b) a major incident occurred; or
(c) the health or safety of any person was endangered and where a dangerous substance was spilled, the uncontrolled release of any substance under pressure took place, machinery or any part thereof fractured or failed resulting in flying, falling or uncontrolled moving objects, or machinery ran out of control,
shall, within the prescribed period and in the prescribed manner, be reported to an inspector by the employer or the user of the plant or machinery concerned.
(2) In the event of an incident in which a person died, or was injured to such an extent that he is likely to die, or suffered the loss of a limb or part of a limb, no person shall without the consent of an inspector disturb the site at which the incident occurred or remove any article or substance involved in the incident therefrom, except as necessary to prevent a further incident, remove the injured or dead, or rescue persons from danger.
(3) The provisions of subsections (1) and (2) shall not apply in respect of a traffic accident on a public road, an incident occurring in a private household provided the householder forthwith reports the incident to the South African Police, or any accident which is to be investigated under section 12 of the Aviation Act, 1962.
(4) A member of the South African Police to whom an incident was reported shall forthwith notify an inspector thereof.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Report to chief inspector regarding occupational disease
body: Any medical practitioner who examines or treats a person for a disease described in the Second Schedule to the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1941, or any other disease which he believes arose out of that person's employment, shall within the prescribed period and in the prescribed manner report the case to the person's employer and to the chief inspector, and inform that person accordingly.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Victimization forbidden
body:
(1) No employer shall dismiss an employee, or reduce the rate of his remuneration, or alter the terms or conditions of his employment to terms less favourable to him, or alter his position relative to other employees to his disadvantage, by reason of the fact that that employee has given information required under this Act, complied with a lawful direction of an inspector, given evidence before a court of law or the industrial court, or done anything which he may or is required to do in terms of this Act.
(2) No employer shall unfairly dismiss an employee, or reduce the rate of his remuneration, or alter the terms or conditions of his employment to terms less favourable to him, by reason of information the employer has obtained regarding biological monitoring or medical surveillance results, or a report made in terms of section 25.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Designation and functions of chief inspector
body:
(1) The Minister shall designate an officer serving in the Department as chief inspector for the purposes of this Act.
(2) The chief inspector shall perform his functions subject to the control and supervision of the Director-General of the Department and may perform any function assigned to an inspector by this Act.
(3) (a) The chief inspector may delegate any power conferred upon him by this Act to any other officer or authorize any such officer to perform any duty assigned to him by this Act.
(b) No delegation of a power shall prevent the exercise of such power by the chief inspector himself.
(4) Whenever the chief inspector is absent or unable to perform his functions, the Minister may designate any other officer to act as chief inspector.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Designation of inspectors by Minister
body:
(1) The Minister may designate any person as an inspector to perform, subject to the control and directions of the chief inspector, any or all of the functions assigned to an inspector by this Act.
(2) Each inspector designated under subsection (1) shall be furnished with a certificate signed by or on behalf of the Minister and stating that he has been designated as an inspector.
(3) Whenever an inspector performs a function under this Act in the presence of any person affected thereby, the inspector shall on demand by such person produce to him the certificate referred to in subsection (2).

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Functions of inspectors

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Special powers of inspectors
body:
(1) (a) Whenever an employer performs an act which in the opinion of an inspector threatens the health or safety of any person, the inspector may in writing prohibit that employer from continuing or commencing with the performance of that act.
(b) Whenever a user of plant or machinery uses any plant or machinery in a manner which threatens the health or safety of any person, the inspector may in writing prohibit that user from continuing or commencing with the use of such plant or machinery.
(c) An inspector may in writing prohibit an employer from requiring or permitting an employee to be exposed for longer than a specified period to any article, substance, organism or condition which threatens the health or safety of that employee.
(d) A prohibition imposed under paragraph (a), (b) or (c) may at any time be revoked by an inspector in writing if arrangements to his satisfaction have been made to dispose of the threat.
(2) In order to enforce a prohibition imposed under subsection (1)(a) or (b), an inspector may block, bar, barricade or fence off that part of the workplace, plant or machinery to which the prohibition applies, and no person shall interfere with or remove such blocking, bar, barricade or fence.
(3) Whenever an inspector is of the opinion that the health or safety of any person is threatened on account of the refusal or failure of an employer or user to take reasonable steps, the inspector may in writing direct that employer or user to take such steps as are specified within a specified period.
(4) Whenever an inspector is of the opinion that an employer or user has failed to comply with a provision of a regulation, the inspector may in writing direct that employer or user to take within a specified period such steps as are necessary to comply.
(5) A period contemplated in subsection (3) or (4) may at any time be extended by an inspector by notice in writing.
(6) An employer shall forthwith bring the contents of a prohibition, direction or notice under this section to the attention of the health and safety representatives and employees concerned.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Investigations
body:
(1) An inspector may investigate the circumstances of any incident which has resulted, or could have resulted, in the injury, illness or death of any person in order to determine whether it is necessary to hold a formal investigation in terms of section 32.
(2) After completing the investigation the inspector shall submit a written report, together with all relevant statements, documents and information, to the attorney-general within whose area of jurisdiction such incident occurred, and a copy to the chief inspector.
(3) Upon receipt of the report, the attorney-general shall deal therewith in accordance with the Inquests Act, 1959, or the Criminal Procedure Act, 1977, as the case may be.
(4) An inspector holding an investigation shall not incur any civil liability by virtue of anything contained in the report.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Formal inquiries
body:
(1) The chief inspector may, and he shall when so requested by a person producing prima facie evidence of an offence, direct an inspector to conduct a formal inquiry into any incident which has resulted, or could have resulted, in the injury, illness or death of any person.
(2) For the purposes of an inquiry an inspector may subpoena any person to appear before him to give evidence or produce any book, document or thing which has a bearing on the subject of the inquiry.
(3) Save as is otherwise provided, the law governing criminal trials in magistrates' courts shall apply to obtaining the attendance of witnesses, the administering of an oath, their examination, and the production by them of books, documents and things.
(4) Any inquiry under this section shall be held in public, provided the presiding inspector may exclude any person whose presence is, in his opinion, undesirable or not in the public interest.
(5) The presiding inspector may designate any person to lead evidence and examine any witness. Any person with an interest in the issue may personally or by representative, advocate or attorney put questions to a witness. Persons with such interest include the injured party, the employer or user involved, any person who could be held responsible, a relevant trade union, and any owner or occupier of the premises.
(6) An inquiry may be adjourned at any time by the presiding inspector, and may be continued by a different inspector.
(7) An affidavit made by any person in connection with the incident shall at the discretion of the presiding inspector be admissible as proof of the facts stated therein.
(8) Whenever the examination of a witness is necessary but attendance cannot be procured without unreasonable delay, expense or inconvenience, the presiding inspector may appoint a commissioner to take the evidence of such witness.
(9) At the conclusion of an inquiry, the presiding inspector shall compile a written report thereon.
(10) The evidence given at any inquiry shall be recorded and a copy submitted with the report to the chief inspector, and in the case of death or serious injury, to the attorney-general.
(11) Nothing in this section shall be construed as preventing criminal proceedings or the arrest of any person.
(12) Upon receipt of the report, the attorney-general shall deal therewith in accordance with the Inquests Act, 1959, or the Criminal Procedure Act, 1977.
(13) An inspector presiding at any formal inquiry shall not incur any civil liability by virtue of anything contained in the report.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Joint inquiries
body:
(1) The provisions of section 32 shall not affect any law requiring and regulating inquests in case of death resulting from other than natural causes, and an inquiry under section 32 and an inquest held under the Inquests Act, 1959, may be held jointly.
(2) At such a joint inquiry and inquest the judicial officer shall preside, but the inspector and the judicial officer shall each make the report required of them by section 32(9) and the Inquests Act, respectively.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Obstruction of investigation or inquiry or presiding inspector or failure to render assistance

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Appeal against decision of inspector
body:
(1) Any person aggrieved by any decision taken by an inspector may appeal against such decision to the chief inspector, who shall confirm, set aside or vary the decision or substitute any other decision which the inspector ought to have taken.
(2) Any person who wishes to appeal shall within 60 days after the inspector's decision was made known, lodge such an appeal with the chief inspector in writing, setting out the grounds on which it is made.
(3) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the chief inspector may appeal to the Labour Court, which shall confirm, set aside or vary the decision or substitute any other decision which the chief inspector ought to have taken.
(4) Any person who wishes to appeal in terms of subsection (3) shall within 60 days after the chief inspector's decision was given, lodge the appeal with the registrar of the Labour Court.
(5) An appeal under subsection (1) or (3) in connection with a prohibition imposed under section 30(1)(a) or (b) shall not suspend the operation of such prohibition.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Disclosure of information
body: No person shall disclose any information concerning the affairs of any other person obtained by him in carrying out his functions in terms of this Act, except to the extent necessary for the proper administration of a provision of this Act, for the purposes of the administration of justice, or at the request of a health and safety representative or committee entitled thereto.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Acts or omissions by employees or mandataries
body:
(1) Whenever an employee does or omits to do any act which it would be an offence for the employer or a user to do or omit to do, the employer or user shall be presumed to have done or omitted to do that act, unless it is proved that the employee acted without the connivance or permission of the employer, that it was not within the scope of the employee's authority, and that all reasonable steps were taken by the employer to prevent it. The fact that instructions forbidding such an act were issued shall not, in itself, be accepted as sufficient proof of reasonable steps.
(2) The provisions of subsection (1) shall apply in the case of a mandatary of any employer or user, except if the parties have agreed in writing to arrangements ensuring compliance by the mandatary.
(3) Whenever any employee or mandatary does or omits to do an act which would be an offence for the employer or user, he shall be liable to be convicted and sentenced as if he were the employer or user.
(4) The same applies to an employee or mandatary of the State, as if the State were an ordinary employer.
(5) Any employee or mandatary referred to in subsection (3) may be so convicted and sentenced in addition to the employer or user.
(6) Whenever an employee or mandatary is convicted of contravening section 23, the court shall make the relevant order against the employer, not the employee or mandatary.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Offences, penalties and special orders of court
body:
(1) Any person who contravenes or fails to comply with a range of provisions of this Act (including sections 7-26, 29(3), 30, 34 and 36), furnishes false information, hinders or obstructs an inspector, refuses to answer questions, misuses safety equipment, or wilfully or recklessly does anything at a workplace which threatens the health or safety of any person, shall be guilty of an offence and on conviction be liable to a fine not exceeding R50 000 or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding one year or to both.
(2) Any employer or user whose act or omission causes injury to a person, and whose conduct would have amounted to culpable homicide had the injury caused death, shall be guilty of an offence and on conviction be liable to a fine not exceeding R100 000 or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding two years or to both.
(3) Whenever a person is convicted of an offence consisting of a failure to comply with a provision of this Act, the court may, in addition to any punishment, issue an order requiring compliance within a determined period.
(4) Whenever an employer is convicted of contravening section 23, the court shall determine the amount unlawfully deducted and act with respect to it as if it were an amount underpaid under the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1983.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Proof of certain facts
body:
(1) Whenever it is proved that any person was present on or in any premises, that person shall, unless the contrary is proved, be presumed to be an employee.
(2) In the absence of satisfactory proof of age, the age of any person shall be presumed to be that stated by an inspector to be in his opinion the probable age of the person, subject to examination by a district surgeon at the request of an interested party.
(3) Any statement or entry contained in any book or document kept by an employer, user, employee or mandatary shall be admissible in evidence against the employer or user as an admission of the facts set forth, unless proved not to have been made within the scope of authority.
(4) Whenever it is proved that any untrue statement or entry is contained in any record, the person keeping it shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, wilfully to have falsified that record.
(5) At the trial of any person charged with a contravention of section 22, it shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, that the article, substance, plant, machinery or health and safety equipment sold or marketed did not comply with the requirements. A certificate from an approved inspection authority shall be accepted as prima facie proof of the facts stated therein.
(6) Whenever the question arises whether any document contains the text of a health and safety standard incorporated in the regulations under section 44, a statement by an inspector to that effect shall be prima facie proof of the facts stated.
(7) The records to be kept by a health and safety committee in terms of section 20(2) shall on their mere production at any legal proceedings be admissible as evidence that a recommendation or report was made.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Exemptions
body:
(1) The Minister may, for such period and on such conditions as may be determined by him, exempt any employer or user or category thereof from any of or all the provisions of this Act.
(2) The period for which exemption may be granted may commence on a date earlier than the date on which exemption is granted, but not earlier than the date on which application for such exemption was made.
(3) An exemption shall, in the case of a particular employer or user, be granted by issuing a certificate of exemption specifying the scope, period and conditions; in the case of a category of employers or users, be granted by publication in the Gazette.
(4) A certificate of exemption or a notice may at any time be amended or withdrawn by the Minister.
(5) An exemption shall lapse upon termination of the period for which it was granted, or upon withdrawal of the relevant certificate or notice.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: This Act not affected by agreements
body: Subject to the provisions of sections 10(4) and 37(2), a provision of this Act or a condition specified in any notice, direction or exemption issued thereunder, shall not be affected by any condition of any agreement, whether entered into before or after the commencement of this Act.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Delegation and assignment of functions
body:
(1) The Minister may delegate any power conferred upon him by this Act, except the power contemplated in section 43, to an officer.
(2) A delegation shall not prevent the exercise of the relevant power by the Minister himself.
(3) The Minister may authorize any provincial administration or local authority to perform any function referred to in this Act.
(4) An authorization shall not prevent the performance of the relevant function by the Minister, the chief inspector or an inspector.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Regulations
body:
(1) The Minister may make regulations as to any matter which in terms of this Act shall or may be prescribed, and any matter necessary or expedient in the interest of the health and safety of persons at work, including regulations as to the planning, layout, construction, use, alteration, repair, maintenance or demolition of buildings; the design, manufacture, construction, installation, operation, use, handling, alteration, repair, maintenance or conveyance of plant, machinery or health and safety equipment; training and safety equipment to be provided by employers; health, safety and occupational hygiene measures; biological monitoring and medical surveillance; the production, processing, use, handling, storage or transport of hazardous substances and exposure limits; work in hazardous conditions; emergency equipment and first aid; health and safety directives; registration of persons performing hazardous work; accreditation of approved inspection authorities; consultation between employers and employees; provision of information; smoking and eating restrictions; and the manufacture of explosives. Regulations may also cover major hazard installations, registration of premises and of plant and machinery, and the establishment of administrative committees.
(2) No regulation shall be made by the Minister except after consultation with the Council, and no regulation relating to State income or expenditure or to any health matter shall be made except after consultation also with the relevant Ministers.
(3) In making regulations the Minister may apply any method of differentiation that he may deem advisable, provided that no differentiation on the basis of race or colour shall be made.
(4) A regulation may prescribe a penalty of a fine, or imprisonment for a period not exceeding 12 months, and, in the case of a continuous offence, an additional fine of R200 or additional imprisonment of one day for each day the offence continues, not exceeding 90 days in total.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Incorporation of health and safety standards in regulations
body:
(1) The Minister may by notice in the Gazette incorporate in the regulations any health and safety standard, without stating the text thereof, by mere reference to its number, title and year of issue.
(2) No health and safety standard shall be incorporated in the regulations except after consultation with the Council.
(3) Any health and safety standard incorporated in the regulations shall, for the purposes of this Act, be deemed to be a regulation, but not before the expiry of two months from the date of incorporation.
(4) Whenever any health and safety standard is amended or substituted after incorporation, the notice incorporating it shall, unless otherwise stated, be deemed to refer to that standard as so amended or substituted.
(5) The chief inspector shall keep a register of particulars of every publication of an incorporated health and safety standard and make it available free of charge for inspection.
(6) The provisions of section 31 of the Standards Act, 1993, shall not apply to any incorporation of a health and safety standard under this section.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Serving of notices
body: Unless another method is prescribed, a notice under this Act shall be served by delivering a copy to the person, by leaving a copy at their usual or last known place of residence or business, or by sending a copy by registered post to that address.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Jurisdiction of magistrates' courts
body: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law, a magistrate's court shall have jurisdiction to impose any penalty or make any order provided for in this Act, but no magistrate's court shall be competent to pronounce upon the validity of any regulation made under this Act.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: State bound
body: This Act shall bind the State.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Conflict of provisions
body: In so far as any provision of the Explosives Act, 1956, is repugnant to a provision of this Act, the provisions of this Act shall apply.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Repeal of laws
body: The Machinery and Occupational Safety Act, 1983, the Machinery and Occupational Safety Amendment Act, 1989, and the Machinery and Occupational Safety Amendment Act, 1991, are hereby repealed.

collection: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
title: Short title and commencement
body:
(1) This Act shall be called the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993, and shall come into operation on a date fixed by the State President by proclamation in the Gazette.
(2) Different dates may be so fixed in respect of different provisions of this Act.

collection: Construction Regulations, 2014
title: Scope of Application
body:
(1) These Regulations are applicable to all persons involved in construction work.

(2) Regulations 3 and 5 are not applicable where the construction work carried out is in relation to a single storey dwelling for a client who intends to reside in such dwelling upon completion thereof.

collection: Construction Regulations, 2014
title: Application for construction work permit
body:
(1) A client who intends to have construction work carried out, must at least 30 days before that work is to be carried out apply to the provincial director in writing for a construction work permit to perform construction work if the intended construction work will—
(a) exceed 180 days;
(b) will involve more than 1800 person days of construction work; or
(c) the works contract is of a value equal to or exceeding thirteen million rand or Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) grading level 6.

(2) An application contemplated in subregulation (1) must be done in a form similar to Annexure 1.

(3) The provincial director must issue a construction work permit in writing to perform construction work contemplated in subregulation (1) within 30 days of receiving the construction work permit application and must assign a site specific number for each construction site.

(4) A site specific number contemplated in subregulation (3) must be conspicuously displayed at the main entrance to the site for which that number is assigned.

(5) A construction work permit contemplated in this regulation may be granted only if—
(a) the fully completed documents contemplated in regulation 5(1)(a) and (b) have been submitted; and
(b) proof in writing has been submitted—
(i) that the client complies with regulation 5(5)
(ii) with regard to the registration and good standing of the principal contractor as contemplated in regulation 5(1)(j); and
(iii) that regulation 5(1)(c), (d), (e), (f), (g) and (h) has been complied with.

(6) A client must ensure that the principal contractor keeps a copy of the construction work permit contemplated in subregulation (1) in the occupational health and safety file for inspection by an inspector, the client, the client's authorised agent, or an employee.

(7) No construction work contemplated in subregulation (1) may be commenced or carried out before the construction work permit and number contemplated in subregulation (3) have been issued and assigned.

(8) A site specific number contemplated in subregulation (3) is not transferrable.

collection: Construction Regulations, 2014
title: Management and supervision of construction work
body:
(1) A principal contractor must in writing appoint one full-time competent person as the construction manager with the duty of managing all the construction work on a single site, including the duty of ensuring occupational health and safety compliance, and in the absence of the construction manager an alternate must be appointed by the principal contractor.

(2) A principal contractor must upon having considered the size of the project, in writing appoint one or more assistant construction managers for different sections thereof: Provided that the designation of any such person does not relieve the construction manager of any personal accountability for failing in his or her management duties in terms of this regulation.

(3) Where the construction manager has not appointed assistant construction managers as contemplated in subregulation (2), or, in the opinion of an inspector, a sufficient number of such assistant construction managers have not been appointed, that inspector must direct the construction manager in writing to appoint the number of assistant construction managers indicated by the inspector, and those assistant construction managers must be regarded as having been appointed under subregulation (2).

(4) No construction manager appointed under subregulation (1) may manage any construction work on or in any construction site other than the site in respect of which he or she has been appointed.

(5) A contractor must, after consultation with the client and having considered the size of the project, the degree of danger likely to be encountered or the accumulation of hazards or risks on the site, appoint a full-time or part-time construction health and safety officer in writing to assist in the control of all health and safety related aspects on the site: Provided that, where the question arises as to whether a construction health and safety officer is necessary, the decision of an inspector is decisive.

(6) No contractor may appoint a construction health and safety officer to assist in the control of health and safety related aspects on the site unless he or she is reasonably satisfied that the construction health and safety officer that he or she intends to appoint is registered with a statutory body approved by the Chief Inspector and has the necessary competencies and resources to assist the contractor.

(7) A construction manager must in writing appoint construction supervisors responsible for construction activities and ensuring occupational health and safety compliance on the construction site.

(8) A contractor must, upon having considered the size of the project, in writing appoint one or more competent employees for different sections thereof to assist the construction supervisor contemplated in subregulation (7), and every such employee has, to the extent clearly defined by the contractor in the letter of appointment, the same duties as the construction supervisor: Provided that the designation of any such employee does not relieve the construction supervisor of any personal accountability for failing in his or her supervisory duties in terms of this regulation.

(9) Where the contractor has not appointed an employee as contemplated in subregulation (8), or, in the opinion of an inspector, a sufficient number of such employees have not been appointed, that inspector must instruct the employer to appoint the number of employees indicated by the inspector, and those employees must be regarded as having been appointed under subregulation (8).

(10) No construction supervisor appointed under subregulation (7) may supervise any construction work on or in any construction site other than the site in respect of which he or she has been appointed: Provided that if a sufficient number of competent employees have been appropriately designated under subregulation (7) on all the relevant construction sites, the appointed construction supervisor may supervise more than one site.

collection: Construction Regulations, 2014
title: Risk assessment for construction work
tags: risk assessment hazard identification method statement
body:
(1) A contractor must, before the commencement of any construction work and during such construction work, have risk assessments performed by a competent person appointed in writing, which risk assessments form part of the health and safety plan to be applied on the site, and must include—
(a) the identification of the risks and hazards to which persons may be exposed to;
(b) an analysis and evaluation of the risks and hazards identified based on a documented method;
(c) a documented plan and applicable safe work procedures to mitigate, reduce or control the risks and hazards that have been identified;
(d) a monitoring plan; and
(e) a review plan.

(2) A contractor must ensure that as far as is reasonably practicable, ergonomic related hazards are analyzed, evaluated and addressed in a risk assessment.

(3) A contractor must ensure that all employees under his or her control are informed, instructed and trained by a competent person regarding any hazard and the related work procedures and or control measures before any work commences, and thereafter at the times determined in the risk assessment monitoring and review plan of the relevant site.

(4) A principal contractor must ensure that all contractors are informed regarding any hazard that is stipulated in the risk assessment before any work commences, and thereafter at the times that may be determined in the risk assessment monitoring and review plan of the relevant site.

(5) A contractor must consult with the health and safety committee or, if no health and safety committee exists, with a representative trade union or representative group of employees, on the monitoring and review of the risk assessments of the relevant site.

(6) A contractor must ensure that copies of the risk assessments of the relevant site are available on site for inspection by an inspector, the client, the client's agent, any contractor, any employee, a representative trade union, a health and safety representative or any member of the health and safety committee.

(7) A contractor must review the relevant risk assessment—
(a) where changes are effected to the design and or construction that result in a change to the risk profile; or
(b) when an incident has occurred.

title: Rope access work
tags: working at heights rope access harness supervisor
body:
(1) A contractor must—
(a) appoint a competent person in writing as a rope access supervisor with the duty of supervising all rope access work on the site, including the duty of ensuring occupational health and safety compliance in relation to rope access work: Provided that the appointment of any such person does not relieve the construction manager of any personal accountability for failing in his management duties in terms of this regulation;
(b) ensure that all rope access work on the construction site is carried out under the supervision of a competent person; and
(c) ensure that all rope access operators are competent and licensed to carry out their work.

(2) No contractor may use or allow the use of rope access work unless—
(a) the design, selection and use of the equipment and anchors comply with the safety standards incorporated for this purpose into these Regulations under section 44 of the Act; and
(b) he or she is in possession of a site specific fall protection plan developed by a competent person applicable to the specific work and environment prior to the commencement of the work, including records of maintenance and inspections of all the equipment used for the work operations.

(3) A contractor must ensure that adequate measures are in place to allow rescue procedures to commence immediately in the event of a fall incident taking place.

collection: Construction Regulations, 2014
title: Material hoists
body:
(1) A contractor must ensure that every material hoist and its tower have been constructed in accordance with the generally accepted technical standards and are strong enough and free from defects.

(2) A contractor must ensure that the tower of every material hoist is—
(a) erected on firm foundations and secured to the structure or braced by steel wire guy ropes, and extends to a distance above the highest landing to allow a clear and unobstructed space of at least 900 millimetres for over travel;
(b) enclosed on all sides at the bottom, and at all floors where persons are at risk of being struck by moving parts of the hoist, except on the side or sides giving access to the material hoist, with walls or other effective means to a height of at least 2100 millimetres from the ground or floor level; and
(c) provided with a door or gate at least 2100 millimetres in height at each landing, and that door or gate must be kept closed except when the platform is at rest at such a landing.

(3) A contractor must cause—
(a) the platform of every material hoist to be designed in a manner that it safely contains the loads being conveyed and that the combined mass of the platform and the load does not exceed the designed lifting capacity of the hoist;
(b) the hoisting rope of every material hoist which has a remote winch to be effectively protected from damage by any external cause to the portion of the hoisting rope between the winch and the tower of the hoist; and
(c) every material hoist to be provided with an efficient brake capable of holding the platform with its maximum load in any position when power is not being supplied to the hoisting machinery.

(4) No contractor may require or permit trucks, barrows or material to be conveyed on the platform of a material hoist and no person may so convey trucks, barrows or material unless those articles are secured or contained in a manner that displacement thereof cannot take place during movement.

(5) A contractor must cause a notice, indicating the maximum mass load which may be carried at any one time and the prohibition of persons from riding on the platform of the material hoist, to be affixed around the base of the tower and at each landing.

(6) A contractor of a material hoist may not require or permit any person to operate a hoist, unless the person is competent in the operation of that hoist.

(7) No contractor may require or permit any person to ride on a material hoist.

(8) A contractor must ensure that every material hoist—
(a) is inspected on daily basis by a competent person appointed in writing by the contractor and such competent person must have the experience pertaining to the erection and maintenance of material hoists or similar machinery;
(b) inspection contemplated in paragraph (a), includes the determination of the serviceability of the entire material hoist, including guides, ropes and their connections, drums, sheaves or pulleys and all safety devices;
(c) inspection results are entered and signed in a record book by a competent person, which book must be kept on the premises for that purpose;
(d) is properly maintained and the maintenance records in this regard are kept on site.

collection: Construction Regulations, 2014
title: Bulk mixing plant
tags: bulk mixing plant confined space silo
body:
(1) A contractor must ensure that the operation of a bulk mixing plant is supervised by a competent person who has been appointed in writing and is—
(a) aware of all the dangers involved in the operation thereof; and
(b) conversant with the precautionary measures to be taken in the interest of health and safety.

(2) No person supervising or operating a bulk mixing plant may authorize any other person to operate the plant, unless that person is competent to operate a bulk mixing plant.

(3) A contractor must ensure that the placement and erection of a bulk mixing plant complies with the requirements set out by the manufacturer and that such plant is erected as designed.

(4) A contractor must ensure that all devices to start and stop a bulk mixing plant are provided and that those devices are—
(a) placed in an easily accessible position; and
(b) constructed in a manner to prevent accidental starting.

(5) A contractor must ensure that the machinery and plant selected is suitable for the mixing task and that all dangerous moving parts of a mixer are placed beyond the reach of persons by means of doors, covers or other similar means.

(6) No person may remove or modify any guard or safety equipment relating to a bulk mixing plant, unless authorized to do so by the appointed person contemplated in subregulation (1).

(7) A contractor must ensure that all precautionary measures stipulated for confined spaces as determined in the General Safety Regulations, are complied with when entering any silo.

(8) A contractor must ensure that a record is kept of all repairs or maintenance to a bulk mixing plant and that the record is available on site to an inspector, the client, the client's agent or any employee.

title: Recording and investigation of incidents
tags: incident register investigation health and safety committee
body:
(1) An employer or user shall keep at a workplace or section of a workplace, as the case may be, a record in the form of Annexure 1 for a period of at least three years, which record shall be open for inspection by an inspector, of all incidents which he or she is required to report in terms of section 24 of the Act and also of any other incident which resulted in the person concerned having had to receive medical treatment other than first aid.

(2) An employer or user shall cause every incident, which must be recorded in terms of subregulation (1), to be investigated by the employer, a person appointed by him or her, by a health and safety representative or a member of a health and safety committee within 7 days from the date of the incident and finalised as soon as is reasonably practicable, or within the contracted period in the case of contracted workers.

(3) The employer or user shall cause the findings of the investigation contemplated in subregulation (2) to be entered in Annexure 1 immediately after completion of such investigation.

(4) An employer shall cause every record contemplated in subregulation (1) to be examined by the health and safety committee for that workplace or section of the workplace at its next meeting and shall ensure that necessary actions, as may be reasonable practicable, are implemented and followed up to prevent the recurrence of such incident.

collection: General Administrative Regulations, 2003
title: Witness at inquiry
body:
(1) When an inspector is directed to hold a formal inquiry into an incident in terms of section 32(1) of the Act, he or she shall notify the employer or user concerned of the date, time and place of such inquiry.

(2) The employer or user shall forthwith advise in writing those persons who witnessed an incident, the union recognised by him or her and any other person specified by the inspector, of such date, time and place, and that their presence shall be required at the inquiry.

(3) The employer or user concerned shall ascertain which of the persons he or she has advised in terms of subregulation (2) are likely to refuse to attend the inquiry, and shall forthwith advise the inspector of the names and addresses of such persons in for the inspector to subpoena such persons.

(4) A subpoena issued in terms of section 32(2) of the Act shall be in the form of Annexure 2: Provided that, when a subpoena is served personally on a person, the service of such subpoena may be effected by any person authorised thereto by the inspector who has signed it.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Emergency equipment, medicine and first aid
tags: first aid box emergency eyewash deluge shower
body:
(1) An employer shall provide a first-aid box or boxes at or near a workplace which shall be available and accessible for the treatment of injured persons at that workplace.

(2) The employer shall stock the first-aid box with suitable up-to-date first aid equipment, taking into account the type of injuries likely to occur, the nature of activities, and the number of persons employed.

(3) In a workplace situated in a multi-storey building, or consisting of more than one building, the employer shall ensure persons can receive prompt first aid treatment.

(4) Where more than 10 employees are employed at any workplace, the employer shall ensure that for every group of up to 100 employees at least one person holding a valid first aid certificate of competency (issued or endorsed by the SA Red Cross Society, St John Ambulance, SA Noodhulpliga, or an inspector-approved body) is readily available during working times.

(5) The first aid worker shall be trained in and acquainted with first aid measures for acute poisoning by, or spillage or leakage of, any dangerous or high-risk substance handled at that workplace.

(6) The employer shall indicate the first aid worker's name on the first-aid box, and clearly indicate the location of every first-aid box by means of a sign.

(7) Any person suffering an open wound, cut, abrasion, sore or similar injury who works where a high-risk, toxic, corrosive or infectious substance is used, handled, processed or produced shall report such injury at the earliest opportunity, and shall be treated before continuing work.

(8) Nothing other than first aid equipment or similar emergency equipment or medicine shall be kept in a first-aid box.

(9) Where an employee is exposed to a potential eye injury hazard from a biological, chemical or physical agent, the employer shall provide an eyewash-fountain supplied with clean water, or similarly effective facility, at or near that workplace.

(10) Where an employee is exposed to a potential skin injury or absorption hazard from a toxic, corrosive or high-risk substance, the employer shall provide a quick-acting deluge-shower supplied with clean water, or equivalent, at or near that workplace.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Use and storage of flammable liquids
tags: flammable liquids spraying storage ventilation fire
body:
(1) No employer shall require or permit any person to work in a place where flammable liquid vapour constitutes an actual or potential fire or explosion hazard, unless the provisions of subregulations (2) to (12) are complied with.

(2) A flammable liquid may only be used or applied in a fire-resisting room, cabinet or enclosure (2-hour fire-resistance), or a place where no fire or explosion hazard is created, vapour is efficiently dispersed, and no other workplace is contaminated.

(3) Every such room, cabinet or enclosure shall be fitted with an efficient intake and exhaust ventilation system; employees doing spraying must be provided with, and must use, an approved respirator, mask or breathing apparatus.

(4)–(7) Ventilation and construction requirements are prescribed for spraying rooms, cabinets and enclosures, including minimum air speeds and fire-resistant ducting.

(8)(a) No fire, flame, naked light, static-generating item, or any ignition source may be used or taken into any room, cabinet or enclosure where flammable liquid is used, sprayed or stored; smoking is prohibited in any such place; conspicuous warning signs must be displayed at entrances.

(9) Discarded cotton waste, cleaning rags or similar material must be removed daily; only one day's quantity of flammable liquid may be kept in the room; all containers must be kept tightly closed when not in use.

(10) Every flammable liquid store shall be fire-separated (2-hour fire-resistance) from spraying areas, constructed to contain spillage plus 10%, ventilated to prevent vapour accumulation, and clearly marked.

(11) An employer shall install adequate fire-fighting equipment in and around every building where flammable liquids are used, handled or stored, as recommended by the local fire chief.

(12) For building work, flammable liquids must be used so that no fire or explosion hazard is created and the workplace is effectively ventilated; where ventilation is not possible, employees must be provided with and use approved respiratory protection.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Work in confined spaces
tags: confined space entry breathing apparatus rescue oxygen
body:
(1) An employer or user of machinery shall ensure a confined space is entered only after the air has been tested and certified safe in writing by a competent person, considering the nature and duration of the work.

(2) Where subregulation (1) cannot be complied with, and a hazardous gas, vapour, dust, fumes, or oxygen content below 20% by volume exists or is likely, entry is only permitted when the space is purged/ventilated and isolated from all pipes, ducts and openings by effective blanking (or locked valves/cocks).

(3) Where subregulation (2)(a) cannot be complied with, entry is only permitted using approved breathing apparatus, with a safety harness and attended rope, at least one other trained person in attendance outside, and breathing/resuscitation apparatus available immediately outside.

(4) All persons must vacate the confined space on completion of work.

(5) Where hazardous gas, vapour, dust or fumes are explosive or flammable, entry is only permitted if the concentration does not exceed 25% of the lower explosive limit (non-ignition-source work) or 10% (other work).

(6) These provisions also apply, as far as practicable, to work performed near or bordering a confined space where hazardous conditions may occur.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Work in elevated positions
tags: working at heights ladder scaffolding elevated position
body: No employer shall require or permit any person to work in an elevated position, and no person shall work in an elevated position, unless such work is performed safely from a ladder or scaffolding, or from a position where such person has been made as safe as if he were working from scaffolding.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Working in danger of engulfment
body:
No employer shall require or permit any person to, and no person shall, enter any place from or into which solid or particulate material is being discharged where a danger exists of a person being engulfed, unless—
(a) such a person is provided with and properly uses a safety belt and rope;
(b) at least one other properly instructed person remains in attendance outside to keep the person under continuous observation and render assistance in an emergency; and
(c) the precautions prescribed by regulation 5 are taken if dangerous gas, fumes, dust or vapour may be present.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Stacking of articles
body:
(1) No employer shall permit the building of tiered stacks unless the operation is properly supervised, the base is level and can sustain the weight, lower tiers can sustain articles above them, tiers are consistent, pallets/containers are in good condition, and any support structure is sound.

(2) Articles may only be removed from the topmost tier; climbing onto a stack is only permitted if stable and done with a ladder or other safe means.

(3) Employers must ensure stacking workers stay clear of hazardous machinery, unstable stacks are dismantled safely, and stack stability isn't endangered by passing vehicles or machinery.

(4) Tiers of sacks, cases, cartons, tins or similar containers must be secured in header-and-stretcher fashion with bonded corners, and stepped back appropriately for stability, unless of regular shape and within permitted height-to-base ratios.

(5) Free-standing stacks built with machinery may, with inspector approval, be built higher provided they remain stable, do not overhang, and the machine operator is protected from falling articles.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Welding, flame cutting, soldering and similar operations
tags: welding flame cutting hot work confined space
body:
(1) Welding or flame cutting may only be undertaken if the operator is fully instructed in safe operation and hazards, effective protection is provided for eyes, respiratory system, face, hands, feet, legs, body and clothing, leads and electrode holders are effectively insulated, and the workplace is partitioned off or other persons are warned and protected.

(2) In a confined space, welding or flame cutting requires effective ventilation, or masks/hoods maintaining a safe air supply.

(3) Electric welding in wet or damp places, inside metal vessels, or in contact with large metal masses requires sound electrical lead insulation, an insulated electrode holder, insulated boots/gloves/mats for the welder, and at least one other trained person in attendance (except where maximum voltage to earth does not exceed 50 volts).

(4) Welding, flame cutting, grinding, soldering or similar work on a closed tube, tank, drum, vessel or container, or one containing substances that may ignite, explode or form dangerous substances under heat, requires prior written certification by a competent person that the danger has been removed.

(5) Where hot work is carried out outside a designated area, the employer must ensure proper and adequate fire precautions are taken.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Operating trains
body:
(1) Employers operating a train or tramway-trucks must station a signalman with a red flag/light, or provide other adequate warning means, at every level crossing.

(2) Trains may not exceed 10 km/h over such crossings.

(3) No person may drive a locomotive unless authorised by their employer.

(4) A locomotive conveying persons (other than those required for its working) may only be driven by the holder of a locomotive engine driver's certificate, subject to the exception in subregulation (5).

(5) A non-steam locomotive with a design speed not exceeding 20 km/h may be driven by an authorised person aged 18 or over, provided their sight, hearing and general fitness are adequate and they are competent.

(6) This regulation does not apply to trains operated by the South African Transport Services.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Supervision of building work
body:
(1) Every employer performing building work shall charge a full-time designated employee with supervising that work (unless the employer has the required experience and supervises personally).

(2) The designated employee must have at least two years' experience in that type of building work.

(3) The employer may designate subordinate employees to assist, without relieving the primary designated employee of accountability; an inspector may require additional subordinate employees to be designated if the number is insufficient.

collection: General Safety Regulations, 1986 (as amended 2025)
title: Roof work
tags: roof work ladders duckboards safety belt
body: Every employer shall provide, and cause to be used, suitable roof-ladders, duck-boards or crawling-boards for persons working on any roof with an unsafe pitch or surface, or that is covered or to be covered with material through which a person could fall: Provided that suitable safety belts attached to the structure, or similarly effective equipment, may be used instead on pitched roofs covered with non-fragile material.
